title: Harness selection and execution — Grove caller views
intro: Homebrew skill delivery is proposed by homebrew-delivery-design-k216, and ravel-default-skill-directory-k218 settled Ravel's default skill directory: Homebrew installs every skill source, and Ravel is the only route that delivers a skill. Owner skill delivery and the coordinated release are reviewed and integrated: one complete Ravel 2.0.0, first through ravel@2, followed by compatible Grove and unversioned promotion. The owner switch's recovery rests on cells, a run record and detection of outside writes, with a Quint model. native-settings-recovery-k221 proposes the gate of the preludes in step 3 and the settings record. Graphs begin at Start here; sequences at their first message; states at their initial state.

groups.title: Coordinated release
groups.description: Publication order owned by this grove; implementation and release remain ahead.

groups.title: Owner skill cutover
groups.description: Proposed: move the owner's installed skills to Ravel sources, keep native capabilities, switch inside finish.

groups.title: User-managed skill delivery
groups.description: User choice of delivery on three supported Ravel routes, subject to actual read access; no named-skill resolver in Grove or Ravel.

groups.title: Independent ownership
groups.description: Grove and Ravel meet at a public CLI. Grove launches ravel as an ordinary child, and Ravel keeps its own runner and release.

groups.title: Public process behavior
groups.description: Ravel routes and supervises, then returns an opaque argument after cleanup. Its own spec owns private runtime mechanics.

groups.title: Grove interpretation
groups.description: Grove owns launch admission, instructions, teardown and the meanings of grove-continue and grove-force-stop.

groups.title: Caller-owned creator evidence
groups.description: Grove policy assets and committed task receipts supply review evidence. Ravel supplies no store or run identity.

diagrams.title: Where each installed entry goes
diagrams.caption: Proposed. Only native copies of owner-selected guidance move to Ravel; a skill that needs a hook keeps a native route for that part.

diagrams.title: Skill formulae outside Ravel
diagrams.caption: Proposed by homebrew-delivery-design-k216 and amended by ravel-default-skill-directory-k218. mise declares each skill formula, and Homebrew installs it. An advance unlinks the earlier keg, installs the new keg and then links it, so a capture reads one complete keg or finds the source absent. A launch during that installation delivers the other sources: a missing superpowers refuses through the mandatory file, and a missing grove makes the session force-stop. A failed offline download leaves the earlier keg in place, and mac-check reports drift.

diagrams.title: Ordered owner cutover
diagrams.caption: Proposed. Ordinary leaves prepare and rehearse; only finish, or the owner after an unsuccessful finish, runs the switch against the real HOME. Each run starts at step 1. Step 3 reads the run record first: while the latest complete backup's run is open, no prelude runs. Otherwise the native settings write a settings record and then exchange in the off value, so Ravel 2.0 delivers no keg source before the switch changes skills, and each later check reports a flagged kept copy. The hooks installation then names only writing-hooks. It runs each Claude Code command under a held link, which keeps a write in place inside the command's interval. It disables the plugin by the exchange after a settings record. It also disables a plugin that an interrupted run left enabled. A rename by another program inside a command's interval is the accepted case. Step 3 then reads the state from the layout, the run record of the latest backup and the plan. A native state switches after a native probe, an interrupted state resumes the inverse, and an active state completes its probes and receipt. A drifted or changed state changes nothing and stops for the owner. One program applies the parts; each exchange records what its displaced copy must hold, so an outside write is kept and reported. The inverse returns the skills cell to the off value. A receipt counts only while each cell is switched, and step 14 copies it into the manual only while each entry outside the switch set matches the plan. The owner purges retained bytes later, after this driver's reap.

diagrams.title: States of the owner switch
diagrams.caption: Proposed, with its focused review integrated. Step 3 reads exactly one state from the layout, the run record and the plan, after the preludes when no run is open. Only an open run whose switched parts form a prefix of the plan's order is interrupted, and only it resumes without the owner. A drifted or changed state changes nothing. The Quint model docs/models/owner-switch.qnt checks the rows and the gate of the preludes; the arrows are a reading aid, not the checked relation.

diagrams.title: Finish keeps its guidance through the switch
diagrams.caption: Proposed. Disabling neither updates nor uninstalls a plugin, so its cache version receives no orphan marker and finish's absolute-path reads survive. The switch runs right after promotion. While no run is open, its step 3 runs the native settings, which write the off value after a settings record, and then the hooks installation, which names only writing-hooks and never refreshes linkuistics. Each of its Claude Code commands runs under a held link, and the disabling is an exchange after a settings record. The switched settings name only the mandatory file, so probe launches capture the keg sources from Ravel's default skill directory.

diagrams.title: Compatible tap states
diagrams.caption: Designed A–D states; implementation and acceptance remain ahead. Installing keg-only ravel@2 changes no default command. Promotion requires compatible published Grove and verified fresh-install and upgrade paths. It moves default users from policy.ts to config.rhai and deprecates ravel@2 at the promoted version. Retained old callers keep complete prefixes and settings.

diagrams.title: Publication and finish ownership
diagrams.caption: This grove owns the release prerequisites while other workstreams stay paused. Cut Ravel once; validate its tagged book and all archives before publishing tag/assets, book, then ravel@2. Finish confirms its full sequence, releases Grove, then promotes Ravel and completes assigned activation. Each failure stops at its recovery boundary. Record teardown and use the original 1.1.0 ending command; retain old resources until readers end.

diagrams.title: Supported Ravel routes
diagrams.caption: Grove implements the admission and both native routes. It supports the directory route through the lifecycle caller and the standalone caller. Grove's version probe decides admission only. The configuration file and Ravel's source set select the route, and Grove reads neither. Without sources in the settings, Ravel 2.0 delivers the keg sources of its default skill directory; "sources": [] gives the native route. The default belongs to the installation, so a separate HOME does not isolate it. A missing configured or mandatory source refuses before any worker, and the leaf stays live. Directory delivery needs 2.0.0, its actual minimum. Native 2.0 and directory 2.0 are separate proofs over the same executable. Until promotion, 2.0.0 is the keg-only ravel@2, which the PATH of the invocation selects.

diagrams.title: Homebrew installs, Ravel delivers
diagrams.caption: Proposed by homebrew-delivery-design-k216. Homebrew links each source into Ravel's default skill directory, which Ravel's installation record names, so brew install and brew upgrade are the whole skill setup. Ravel's skill discovery specification owns the default. A session that its user opens directly sees no Linkuistics skill. Missing mandated guidance ends with force-stop.

diagrams.title: Preserving readers through adoption
diagrams.caption: Target design, not completed rollout. Ravel 2.0.0 publishes first as ravel@2, compatible Grove follows, and finish promotes the same archives. Every intermediate tap dependency remains compatible. Cleanup is optional and manual. Existing session ending commands remain valid; old callers retain compatible prefixes and settings.

diagrams.title: Independent caller and process-manager boundary
diagrams.caption: Separate prefixes and versions, ordinary caller imports, Grove's shared job function and Ravel's own runner. Grove ships TypeScript caller assets for 1.x and Rhai caller assets for 2.x. No shared Rust library or bundled Ravel worker. Ravel alone gives the cleanup assurance.

diagrams.title: Route, supervise and return an argument
diagrams.caption: Optional directory injection on 2.0.0 precedes selection. The prepared prompt wraps the intact mandate once, and originalPrompt holds its exact bytes. The agent finds the named skill using the user-selected route. Refusal launches nothing; successful cleanup returns only the opaque result.

diagrams.title: Two nested jobs and terminal ownership
diagrams.caption: Grove launches ravel as its foreground job and sends a caught TERM or HUP to ravel alone. Ravel manages the harness job and its cleanup. Each supervisor takes the terminal back from its own child. Descendants that escape a group are outside its cleanup guarantee.

diagrams.title: Observable session result lifecycle
diagrams.caption: A reading aid for public behavior, not a checked model or a description of private transport. A published result can succeed despite the managed process later exiting nonzero.

diagrams.title: Lifecycle and standalone callers
diagrams.caption: Both callers use one shared job function and may receive directory hints. Exact caller ending commands remain intact. Lifecycle and standalone result meanings stay unchanged.

diagrams.title: Grove post-reap decision order
diagrams.caption: Epoch invalidation gates interpretation. A failed spawn or wait reads no disposition. After any error, Grove reports it and dies of a caught signal. Driver interruption precedes successful exact force-stop, then teardown, then successful exact continuation. Grove checks no process group after the reap. Force-stop exits 1 without undoing teardown.

diagrams.title: Creator evidence and rejected alternatives
diagrams.caption: Inline selected receipts or explicit owner declarations avoid a store namespace and preserve finishing-attempt origin. They are same-user attestations.

diagrams.title: Finishing producer pins evidence for review
diagrams.caption: Grove caller assets wrap selection and read committed task evidence. Retirement renames only; the finishing session writes Creator lines and commits them.

diagrams.title: Configured review selection from caller evidence
diagrams.caption: The configured-review branch of Grove's opt-in policy. Nonreview routing is outside this view. Missing/invalid/legacy evidence or a same-provider route refuses.

discussion.title: Claude Code's own writes in the hooks installation
discussion.status: Proposed by hooks-installation-writes-k222 on 2026-11-06. It settles the open question of native-settings-recovery-k221, and native-settings-recovery-k224 integrated the focused review of both leaves
discussion.summary: Each command of the hooks installation replaces ~/.claude/settings.json by a rename. On an idle machine, the rename came 30 to 38 ms after the read that the command writes from. Each Claude Code command therefore runs under a held link. That is a hard link to the live inode in a settings record, and the program compares it with its digest after the command. The program stops for an ACL or an extended attribute in the reading that the digest covers. A write in place inside the interval, or a later write through a descriptor, flags that copy. The disabling is now the program's own exchange after a settings record, because plugin disable changes only that cell. A rename by another program inside a command's interval is the accepted case. Nothing bounds that interval or the runs of the commands, and the owner design states the evidence.

updatedDiagrams.summary: Each Claude Code command of the hooks installation runs under a held link, and the disabling is an exchange. A flagged held copy leads to the pending record.
The hooks installation writes the real HOME settings. Each command runs under a held link, and the disabling is an exchange.
